A6 (2026-08-27, commit 3069afb): IDockerEngine.ListVolumesAsync (IDockerEngine.cs) is the enumeration that did not exist anywhere -- implemented for real via Docker.DotNet in DockerEngine.cs (used both in-process and inside Harbora.Agent), proxied over the older inbound agent by RemoteDockerEngine.cs against a new GET /agent/volumes. DiskVolumeOrphanReport.cs walks every registered server through IServerEngineFactory, lists its disk, and diffs against Volume rows scoped to MountPath.HarboraVolumePrefix, reached at GET /servers/disk-volume-report (ServersController.cs, Capabilities.ServersManage). Every server is named as Reached, Refused or Unreachable -- never folded into a silent total; DiskVolumeOrphanReportTests.cs and ServersDiskVolumeReportHttpTests.cs pin that. The risk below was real: NodeWorkloadEngine.ListVolumesAsync throws NodeCapabilityException by name (no ListVolumes verb in the v1 node contract, Harbora.NodeAgent.Contracts/NodeCommands.cs) rather than reporting unsupported silently, so a v1 node's disk still cannot be checked -- that is the remaining half. statusEvidence: DatabaseGrantExecutor now resolves its engine per service.ServerId through IServerEngineFactory (src/Harbora.Infrastructure/Services/DatabaseGrantExecutor.cs RunAsync) instead of taking IDockerEngine directly, so a grant's one-off client runs on whichever server actually holds the database - proven for a reachable remote engine (old-style inbound agent) by DatabaseGrantExecutorHostTests.A_database_on_another_reachable_server_runs_the_client_there_not_on_the_panel. An unreachable server (no agent endpoint/no enrolled node) and a v1 node's missing one-off-container verb (NodeCapabilityException, NodeWorkloadEngine.RunOneOffAsync) are each refused by name rather than attempted locally or reported as a generic dropped connection - see A_server_that_cannot_be_resolved_becomes_a_named_refusal_not_an_exception and A_node_with_no_one_off_verb_is_refused_by_name_not_as_a_lost_connection in the same file. AdminerService was changed the same way (src/Harbora.Infrastructure/Services/AdminerService.cs OpenAsync/SweepAsync) and ExternalAccessAvailability.Refuse gained a serviceRunsElsewhere flag wired from DatabasesController/DatabaseAccessActions.cs, so the access page and the admin-tool button both stop offering a database on another server rather than letting DockerTcpGateway's later refusal be the first sign of it - see AdminerServiceHostTests and the new DatabaseAccessPageTests/ExternalAccessAvailabilityTests cases. What remains open, and is the reason this is 'partial' rather than 'done': unlike a grant, Adminer needs a browser-reachable route, and this panel's proxy only ever addresses a container by name on its own Docker networks - so a database on a genuinely remote server (not this panel's own machine) is refused, correctly and by name, rather than made reachable. That gap is exactly the one this backlog entry's own risks field already named ('Adminer needs a published route to a container on another host, which the tunnel work owns') and is unchanged by this pass; closing it needs the ingress/tunnel mechanism NodeIngressRouter already provides for ordinary app deployments (src/Harbora.Infrastructure/Nodes/NodeIngressRouter.cs), wired onto a one-off Adminer session, which is a separate piece of work.

statusEvidence: The core leak (an unfindable orphaned restore dump) is fixed differently than the acceptance criteria prescribe: staging directories are now named deterministically from the restore job's own id (commit 68c02071, BackupStagingLayout.DatabaseRestoreDirectory(job.Id)), so the reconciler can always find and sweep it on the next restart (tests/Harbora.Tests/BackupCrashRecoveryTests.cs:319). But RestoreJob.StagingPath itself was never added, and unlike BackupSnapshot.StagingPath (a persisted pointer retried across restarts if delete fails), a restore row settled to Failed has no persisted retry pointer -- a delete that fails on a busy mount is not retried on a later boot, and nothing tests that gap.
title: RestoreJob has no StagingPath, so a restore's staged copy has no retry pointer
problem: BackupSnapshot carries StagingPath as a standing claim that a plaintext copy still exists at that path, and the module reconciler sweeps from it and retries what it cannot remove. RestoreJob has no such column, so a restore's downloaded dump is cleaned up only by whatever the process managed before it died.
userValue: No plaintext database dump is left behind by a restore that was interrupted.
operationalValue: Gives restores the durable cleanup claim backups already have.
acceptanceCriteria: RestoreJob.StagingPath is written before the dump is staged and cleared when it is removed

The narrower half of this, a table silently unswept because its retention was set to an unusable number, was closed by naming each such table in its own log line.

title: Adminer's route save and proxy apply are outside its own failure path
problem: AdminerService.OpenAsync withdraws the session properly when ApplyAllAsync RETURNS a failure - route removed, container removed, config republished, all on CancellationToken.None. But SaveChangesAsync(ct) and ApplyAllAsync(..., ct) are themselves unguarded, and ct here is a web request's token, cancelled by the operator navigating away. Cancel between the two and an enabled basic-auth route is committed pointing at a throwaway container, with the withdrawal block never entered. Smaller than it first looked: the container is running by then, so the hourly AdminerSweeper reaps both within the hour. Bounded, not silent, not absent.
userValue: Navigating away from a database page never leaves a published admin host behind.
operationalValue: Closes the last unguarded write on a path that publishes a route.
acceptanceCriteria: A cancellation at the save or the apply withdraws the route and the container the same way a returned failure does
The withdrawal continues to run on CancellationToken.None
A test cancels between the save and the apply and asserts no route row survives
risks: Catching OperationCanceledException here must not swallow shutdown
evidence: the returned-failure path at :126-158 was added by 7dd1d7e and covers only that case
